name: Xenon
occurrence: The rarest stable noble gas in the atmosphere, present at less than 0.1 parts per million.
majorUses: High-intensity xenon arc lamps (film projectors, car headlights)
notableCharacteristics: The first noble gas ever shown to form a real, stable chemical compound (xenon hexafluoroplatinate, in 1962), which overturned the long-held belief that noble gases were completely inert.
whyHere: Its much larger, more loosely held outer electrons make xenon far more polarizable than lighter noble gases, which is exactly what allowed chemist Neil Bartlett to force it into forming a genuine chemical bond in 1962, shattering the 'inert gas' assumption.
didYouKnow: For over 60 years after noble gases were discovered, chemists assumed none of them could ever form compounds — until 1962, when xenon was successfully combined with platinum hexafluoride, rewriting a chunk of inorganic chemistry textbooks.
genZNote: Broke the 'noble gases never react' rule after 60+ years of everyone assuming otherwise. The plot twist nobody saw coming.
